input.plan:
# Engineering blog on kuchup.com

## Why this is worth doing

The internal write-ups in [`docs/reference/`](docs/reference/) are already better than most “we learned a lesson” posts: they have timestamps, Postgres counts, before/after timings, and a clear wrong-hypothesis → evidence → fix arc.

The audience overlap is unusually good. Kuchup’s buyers are **software engineers**. A post about running a fetch worker on `t4g.micro` without dying is product proof, not a topic change.

Do **not** paste [`docs/reference/fetch-thread-exhaustion-incident.md`](docs/reference/fetch-thread-exhaustion-incident.md) (or the others) onto the public site. Those files are ops records: SQL against production, sticky `fetch_problem` cleanup, named scrape targets, internal links. Public posts are rewritten stories that keep the numbers and drop the runbook.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Internal["docs/reference incidents"] --> Rewrite["Public rewrite + sanitization"]
  Rewrite --> Canonical["kuchup.com/engineering"]
  Canonical --> Schema["BlogPosting JSON-LD + sitemap"]
  Canonical --> Syndicate["Dev.to with rel=canonical then HN"]
```

## Editorial thesis

One series, four posts, same voice: **measured production failures on a small box**. Hook with the number; spend the middle on the wrong explanation; end with the rule.

| Order | Public slug | Source of truth | Public hook (keep) | Cut or rewrite |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (ship first) | `/engineering/cant-start-new-thread` | [fetch-thread-exhaustion-incident.md](docs/reference/fetch-thread-exhaustion-incident.md) | 186/394 companies flagged; 357/358 errors were `can't start new thread`; last healthy country run 2026-08-29 | Named ATS URLs, leftover-flag cleanup, Go-rewrite debate as internal politics |
| 2 | `/engineering/678-postgres-round-trips` | [board-load-performance-incident.md](docs/reference/board-load-performance-incident.md) | Germany board ~89s → ~1.7s; 678 DB round-trips for 98 companies | Local-port confusion, `.env` pointing at EC2 |
| 3 | `/engineering/cache-check-in-the-hot-path` | [country-cache-redis-hotpath-incident.md](docs/reference/country-cache-redis-hotpath-incident.md) | Same collapse after a “cache invalidation” fix; Redis in a per-company loop | Process-local cache code dump as the whole post |
| 4 | `/engineering/playwright-hung-for-15-hours` | [fetch-scheduler-timeout-practices.md](docs/reference/fetch-scheduler-timeout-practices.md) | Worker “Up” for 15h; no timeout on `wait_for_fetch_thread()` | Name the hung employer board; panel reap internals |

Skip for v1: [catalog-seed-test-failure.md](docs/reference/catalog-seed-test-failure.md) (pytest folklore) and the Kafka / board-read-model **proposals** (not incidents).

Sanitization rules (same as the public-repo secret policy):

- No Elastic IPs, `DATABASE_URL`, Grafana org IDs, SSH, instance IDs.
- Generalize scrape targets (“one generic Playwright career page”), do not publish employer URLs as the villain.
- Show query *shapes*, not a production investigation playbook.
- Soft CTA only: this worker is why the catalog refreshes every 6 hours → country page or `/how-it-works`. No hard sell in the body.

Voice: the existing incident docs already sound human. Keep that. Do not Hallmark-ify them into “here’s what we learned.” [`design.md`](design.md) already names content pages as **typography only** — that is the layout.

## Where it lives (canonical)

**`https://kuchup.com/engineering`**, not `/blog`.

- Primary nav stays job-seeker (`Product`, `MCP`, `Countries`, … in [`homepage/components/Header.tsx`](homepage/components/Header.tsx)). Put **Engineering** in the footer only so it does not dilute the conversion path.
- Index lists posts (date, title, one-line metric). Each post is a long article with `BlogPosting` JSON-LD, author byline, `datePublished`, canonical apex URL.
- Soft product link at the end; do not interleave visa-job CTAs in the technical sections.

Syndication after the canonical URL is live:

1. Dev.to (or Hashnode) with `canonical_url: https://kuchup.com/engineering/...`
2. One HN submission for post 1 only — the thread-exhaustion number is the Show HN / story hook. Do not dump the series.

## Site plumbing (homepage is static export)

Marketing pages are Next `output: "export"` copied into [`relocation_jobs/static/homepage/`](relocation_jobs/static/homepage/) and served by Flask ([`homepage/next.config.ts`](homepage/next.config.ts), [`homepage/scripts/copy-to-flask.mjs`](homepage/scripts/copy-to-flask.mjs), [`relocation_jobs/web/server.py`](relocation_jobs/web/server.py)).

Today Flask only indexes [`FIXED_MARKETING_PATHS`](relocation_jobs/web/server.py) plus `relocation-jobs-*.html`. Nested `/engineering/...` is not in the sitemap and `_is_marketing_path` will 404 it.

Needed:

- Next routes: `homepage/app/engineering/page.tsx` (index) and `homepage/app/engineering/[slug]/page.tsx` (post).
- Content as markdown + frontmatter under `homepage/content/engineering/` (gray-matter + react-markdown, or MDX). Do **not** add a CMS. Typed TS blobs like [`homepage/lib/country-pages.ts`](homepage/lib/country-pages.ts) also work if you want zero new deps for post 1; switch to markdown once the series is more than one file.
- Flask: treat `/engineering` and `/engineering/<slug>` as marketing paths; resolve both `engineering.html` / `engineering/index.html` and nested `engineering/<slug>.html` (Next nested export uses `index.html` for the parent). `send_from_directory` must allow a nested relative path under `HOMEPAGE_STATIC`.
- [`public_marketing_paths()`](relocation_jobs/web/server.py) / `_sitemap_lastmod` so `/sitemap.xml` lists the index and every post (keep jobs on `/sitemap-jobs.xml` — do not mix).
- [`llms.txt`](relocation_jobs/static/llms.txt) and [`docs/operations/seo-indexing.md`](docs/operations/seo-indexing.md): add engineering URLs to the indexation checklist.
- Tests in [`tests/web/test_public_api.py`](tests/web/test_public_api.py): 200 + cache headers for `/engineering` and one slug; sitemap `<loc>` present; unknown slug 404.

Schema on each post: `BlogPosting` (headline, datePublished, author Person, publisher Organization already in [`homepage/app/layout.tsx`](homepage/app/layout.tsx)). `og:type` article.

## Ship order

1. **Plumbing + post 1 only.** Routing, sitemap, schema, footer link, thread-exhaustion rewrite. Deploy, request indexing for `/engineering` and that slug, then syndicate.
2. Posts 2–4 on the same template (N+1, Redis sequel, 15h hang). Internal docs stay the ops source of truth; public posts can link “this is a public write-up of a production incident” without exposing the markdown files.

Do not build a comments system, newsletter, or `/blog` alias in v1.

function StatRow({ label, value }: { label: string; value: string }) { return ( {label} {value} ); } export function CantStartNewThreadPost() { return (

On 1 September 2026 the production board showed a fetch problem on most companies. It looked like employer career sites, or our scrapers, had died. They had not. The EC2 fetch worker could not start OS threads, so every six-hour country cycle failed in about a second and stamped a sticky “fetch problem” flag on the catalog.

The catalog went stale from 30 August onward.{" "} 186 of 394 companies were flagged. Germany and the Netherlands took most of the hits (85 and 84). Last healthy country runs: 29 August 2026.

What we saw

The worker container was still “Up.” The six-hour loop still ran. Cycles “finished,” so nothing in the process table looked wedged. The board then went red.

Postgres on 1 September 2026, after a week of failures

111/111 is bookkeeping, not a scrape. The pool dies immediately; finalize still sets progress to total. Same-second timestamps across countries are sequential scheduling: each country dies in under a second, so a 16-country cycle completes in about two seconds.

First error: 28 August 12:50 UTC. Spike: 29 August 07:00 —{" "} 173 errors in one hour. Every scheduled country run from 30 August onward failed in about a second.

What it was not

Three wrong explanations were easy to reach for:

  • Employer ATS outages. The error string was the same for almost every company. Career sites do not fail in lockstep like that.
  • “Python asyncio uses too much RAM.” Coroutines are cheap. OS threads (~8 MiB stacks) and Chromium are not.
  • A reason to rewrite the worker in Go. HTTP clients would get cheaper. The browser fallback would cost the same. The bug was the concurrency model, not the language.

We run the worker on a t4g.micro. Low RAM is the{" "} constraint, not the bug. A bigger box would have delayed the same failure.

Nested threads, nested event loops

Fetch already runs in a separate container. The code is not a separate system: the worker imports the same fetch, scrape, and catalog packages as the panel and writes the same Postgres.

The model on 1 September, simplified:

        {`scheduler (one country at a time)
  → OS thread for the country
    → asyncio.run  (event loop #1)
      → ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=4)
        → asyncio.run per company  (event loop #2)
          → HTTP to the career board
          → sometimes Playwright Chromium on yet another thread`}

That is thread-per-company with a nested event loop, not a coroutine pool. Production default was FETCH_SCHEDULE_CONCURRENCY=4. Each of those four workers also sized HTTP limits up to 16.

The sequential path (workers <= 1) already did the right thing: await each company on the country loop. Concurrency 4 never used that path. It opened a ThreadPoolExecutor and called asyncio.run() again inside each worker. 

        {`# per company, inside the pool — the bug
async def _inner():
    async with make_fetch_client(concurrency=http_concurrency) as client:
        return await asyncio.wait_for(
            fetch_and_persist_company(...),
            timeout=company_timeout_seconds(),
        )

msg, new_count = asyncio.run(_inner())`}

RuntimeError: can't start new thread means{" "} pthread_create failed — typically ENOMEM or a PID/nproc limit. It does not mean “asyncio RAM is uncontrollable.”

Some career pages have no JSON API. Those fall through to a sync Chromium scrape via asyncio.to_thread. One in-flight generic company could be: country thread + pool thread + nested event loop + extra thread + a browser. That is the RAM and PID amplifier. It is also why the process was already unable to start threads after days of cycles. On 1 September the pool died before boards ran, so the exception string is the thread error, not a hung browser.

A July hang had already taught us to put timeouts on every blocking boundary. Those timeouts do not bound how many OS threads and browsers exist. This incident is that next failure mode.

Why the board said the company was broken

Any attempt message matching — Error: … set a sticky catalog flag. There was no distinction between “this career board returned garbage” and “this process cannot create a thread.” Operators then debug Greenhouse or Ashby instead of the worker.

Runs also looked complete. companies_done == companies_total , the scheduler logged a finished cycle, duration was ~0s,{" "} new_jobs was 0. The stats table does not show{" "} error_message.

Application logs in Docker are not an archive: they vanish on{" "} docker rm -f. Metrics (disk, RAM, health) did not store fetch errors. Durable evidence was Postgres: per-company attempt rows and country-run summaries. Grouping error_message was enough. 

        {`SELECT LEFT(error_message, 180), COUNT(*)
FROM company_fetch_attempts
WHERE status = 'error'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 2 DESC;`}

What we shipped

On 2 September, country fetch stopped starting a{" "} ThreadPoolExecutor or calling asyncio.run(){" "} per company. The outer country thread remains so the scheduler can join it. Companies run on that thread’s one event loop, bounded by{" "} asyncio.Semaphore, sharing one HTTP client. 

        {`scheduler (one country at a time)
  → OS thread for the country
    → asyncio.run  (one loop)
      → asyncio.Semaphore(workers)   default 2
        → await fetch_and_persist_company(shared client)
          → HTTP; Playwright capped at 1 browser`}
  • Default FETCH_SCHEDULE_CONCURRENCY is 2, not 4. Do not raise it on a t4g.micro without watching RSS.
  • Infra errors such as can't start new thread no longer set the sticky company flag.
  • A failed run no longer marks progress as fully “done.”

We did not rewrite the worker in Go. Fetch is already a separate container. Splitting languages without a job contract would duplicate the ATS parsers and the scrape suite. A queued job table is still on the table; it was not this outage’s fix.

The rule

Timeouts bound how long a unit of work may run. They do not bound how many threads, event loops, and browsers you create while it runs. On a small box, asyncio.run() inside a thread pool is a way to spend the process before the timeout ever fires.

One event loop per country. A semaphore for in-flight companies. Playwright at one. Treat “cannot start a thread” as infrastructure, not as a broken employer.

`/engineering` is live in the homepage export, with one public post rewritten from the thread-exhaustion incident.

**Canonical URLs**
- [https://kuchup.com/engineering](https://kuchup.com/engineering)
- [https://kuchup.com/engineering/cant-start-new-thread](https://kuchup.com/engineering/cant-start-new-thread)

Soft close links to `/how-it-works`. Engineering sits in the footer only, not the job-seeker nav.

**Plumbing**
- Next pages + `BlogPosting` JSON-LD + `rel=canonical`
- Flask serves nested `engineering/*.html` and lists them in `/sitemap.xml` (not the jobs sitemap)

Posts 2–4 from the plan are not written yet; the template is ready. After you deploy, request indexing for those two URLs, then syndicate. I did not commit.

I’ll inventory every incident write-up in the reference docs and pull the date plus how each one was fixed.

These are the incident write-ups in `docs/reference/`, in the order they happened. Dates below are **when it occurred** (the write-up’s “Last updated” is in parentheses).

| When | What broke | How we fixed it | Doc |
|------|------------|-----------------|-----|
| **2026-06-28** | Four pytest failures after “newest first” board tests. Extra company **AAA Older Fetch** leaked into the UK catalog. Production was fine. | `seed_country()` now calls `sync_country_catalog` (full sync, including deletes), not additive upsert. | [catalog-seed-test-failure.md](docs/reference/catalog-seed-test-failure.md) |
| **July 2026** (doc 07-08) | Board looked hung. Germany `GET /api/board` ~89–103s. **678 Postgres round-trips** for 98 companies inside `all_country_labels()`. | In-memory country-label cache; board list omits `description_text`; admin stats load async; skip MCP blobs on board load. Germany → **~1.7s**. | [board-load-performance-incident.md](docs/reference/board-load-performance-incident.md) |
| **2026-07-10** | Scheduled fetch stuck **15+ hours**. Playwright hung on one generic board; `wait_for_fetch_thread()` had **no timeout**. Panel reaped the run as failed while the worker kept waiting. | Layered timeouts (company 300s, country join 2700s, Playwright 90s). Panel must not orphan-reap when it is not the fetch owner. Manual worker restart unblocked that cycle. | [fetch-scheduler-timeout-practices.md](docs/reference/fetch-scheduler-timeout-practices.md) |
| **2026-07-13** | Single-company “Fetch jobs” felt flaky: stale complete UI, board refreshed twice, cards re-animated. | Client fetch **session** (`runId` + phase). Board settles **once** after Yes/No. Serial poll instead of `setInterval`. | [fetch-panel-session.md](docs/reference/fetch-panel-session.md) |
| **2026-07-18** | Sequel to the 678-query incident. Cross-process cache invalidation checked **Redis on every** `country_label()` call. Board back to tens of seconds. | Throttle generation check to **≤ once / 5s**; hot path stays in-memory. Board back to **~1.3–1.7s**. | [country-cache-redis-hotpath-incident.md](docs/reference/country-cache-redis-hotpath-incident.md) |
| **2026-08-28 → 09-02** (first error 08-28; all country runs dead from **08-30**; diagnosed 09-01; fix **09-02**) | **186 / 394** companies flagged. **357 / 358** errors were `can't start new thread`. Nested `ThreadPoolExecutor` + `asyncio.run()` per company. | One event loop + `asyncio.Semaphore`; concurrency default **2**; Playwright cap 1; infra errors no longer set `fetch_problem`. Sticky flags from the outage still need a catalog cleanup. | [fetch-thread-exhaustion-incident.md](docs/reference/fetch-thread-exhaustion-incident.md) |

**Companion, not a second incident:** [fetch-concurrency-model-review.md](docs/reference/fetch-concurrency-model-review.md) (2026-09-06) — what we shipped after the thread outage and why that seam is right.

**Not incidents** (proposals / design): Kafka fetch pipeline, board read-model, multi-user scaling, full SPA UI.

On the public blog, only the thread-exhaustion post is published so far (`/engineering/cant-start-new-thread`). The next three planned public posts are the 678 round-trips, the Redis hot-path sequel, and the 15-hour Playwright hang.
